title: Hybrid-index dimensionality migration: rollback-safe coordination, throttling, and client hints
creator: Asha Patel
description: Plan and implement a rollback-safe migration strategy for changing embedding vector dimensionality across live hybrid indices (indices that temporarily contain mixed-dimension documents). This ticket defines an orchestration pattern, client compatibility hints, index-level throttling, and monitoring/rollback controls so customers experience minimal downtime and predictable cost/latency during dimension transitions.
background: We frequently need to upgrade or change embedding dimensionality for quality or model upgrades (e.g., 512 -> 768) and must reindex existing vectors. Existing playbooks focus on full reindex/offline windows. Customers running production retrieval and reranking cannot afford long write pauses or client-side incompatibility. Additionally, mixed-dimension documents cause ANN library errors and degraded recall if not handled carefully. We need a migration pattern that supports: online ingestion during reindex, partial/shadow index coexistence, client negotiation for vector schema, and automated rollback in case of regressions.
proposed_solution: Introduce a coordinated migration workflow composed of: 1) Dimension-aware 'schema header' added to embedding responses and stored metadata so clients can detect vector dim at read time. 2) Shadow-indexing: create a new index with the new dimension, stream writes to both indices (dual-write) until backfill catch-up. 3) Read routing with compatibility layer: queries routed to appropriate index or to cross-dim fallback that triggers on-the-fly projection or rerank. 4) Shard-level reindex throttling: control reindex concurrency based on ingest velocity and CPU/GPU utilization to limit latency spikes. 5) Canary evaluation using production sampling and quality metrics (recall@k, rerank delta). 6) Automated rollback that flips write routing and drains new index if metrics regress beyond thresholds.
migration_steps: Create new index template with updated dimension and quantization profile
Enable dual-write: client and ingestion pipeline write vectors to both old and new indices (flagged), with idempotent writes
Start shard-by-shard backfill job with adaptive concurrency (initially 2 shards) and monitor latency/cpu/gpu
Expose embedding schema header in API responses: "embedding_dim": <int> and include in index metadata
Implement read-time router that aggregates scores across mixed-dim indices or triggers projection fallback
Run canary queries (1% production traffic) comparing new-index results vs old-index results for precision/recall metrics
If canary passes for 48h and resource impact < threshold, increase backfill concurrency and continue until 100% documents reindexed
Cutover: switch primary read routing to new index, keep old index in read-only for 7 days as safety buffer
After stability window, decommission old index and free storage
If at any point regression detected, initiate rollback procedure to route writes back to old-only and stop backfill
client_adapter_spec: Clients must tolerate per-document embedding_dim metadata in responses. New SDKs will include a lightweight adapter that: 1) Validates embedding_dim on fetch and rejects incompatible local vector operations with clear error messages; 2) When writing, supports an optional 'dual_write' boolean to send vectors to both indices; 3) Implements a 'fallback' mode where if a read encounters mixed dims in search results, it will request cross-dim rerank via the server-side reranker. Additions to REST: header 'X-Embedding-Dim: <int>' and response JSON field 'embedding_dim'. Backwards compatibility: if header absent, assume legacy dimension and log a deprecation warning. Provide migration snippets for Python/Node/Go SDKs in the PR.
rollout_plan: Week 0: Prep - create index template, update SDK spec docs, add feature flags
Week 1: Enable dual-write for internal customers and opt-in beta customers
Week 2: Start shard-level backfill at low concurrency, run canary on 1% traffic
Week 3: Expand canary to 10% if metrics stable, promote more customers to dual-write
Week 4: Full backfill completion and switch read routing during a low-traffic window
Week 5-6: Monitor stability and decommission old index after safety window
monitoring_and_alerting: Create dashboards: reindex progress, per-shard CPU/GPU, per-route p95 latency, dual-write error rate
SLOs: p95 query latency < baseline + 15% during migration, write error rate < 0.1%
Quality alerts: recall@10 drop > 5% vs baseline triggers rollback evaluation
Resource alerts: backfill-induced GPU utilization > 85% for 5m triggers automatic throttle
Automated Canary reports pushed to #embeddings-migration Slack channel hourly
testing_plan: Unit tests for schema header parsing and SDK adapter behavior
Integration tests: dual-write idempotency, read-router correctness in presence of mixed dims
Load test: simulate 3x production ingest while running backfill to validate throttling heuristics
A/B quality experiment comparing old vs new index on historical prompt sets and live canary traffic
Chaos test: kill a backfill worker to validate resumable reindex and graceful degradation
rollback_plan: Rollback is automated via feature flag. If quality or latency thresholds exceeded: 1) Flip write routing to old-only (feature flag), 2) Stop any active backfill jobs, 3) Drain in-flight dual-write buffer and reconcile partial writes, 4) Notify customers and create incident with postmortem template, 5) Reevaluate model/quantization profiles before attempting another migration. All rollback steps executed via an orchestration job with an undo script that exists in infra/ops playbooks.
open_questions: Should we support on-the-fly dimension projection (e.g., PCA) server-side for temporary read compatibility, or prefer strict index separation?
What SLA window is acceptable for customer-facing latency increase during backfill? (current proposal: p95 +15%)
Do we require SDK adapters to be mandatory for all customers before we allow dual-write?
How long should the safety buffer (read-only old index) be retained after cutover by default? (proposal: 7 days)
Does legal/compliance require explicit audit logs for dual-write of PII-linked records?
references: Related Linear tickets: ENG-15801, ENG-32671, ENG-43102
notes: This ticket emphasizes operational safety and client compatibility over a single-shot bulk reindex approach. Keep migration alpha-limited to customers who opt into dual-write until we have 48h of stable canary metrics. Coordinate with solutions engineering for customer communication templates.
